properties.name: Before a decision is settled, reflow2 shows what undoing it would cost, computed from what the design holds: the built and checked work downstream of it, and the decisions it rests on where they are recorded. It never scores the upside
properties.source: Anthony Sligar (who:ajs), dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-10-12: "Let's go with your suggestions" on dec:idea-convexity-in-the-decision-process, option (b)
properties.statement:
When a person is about to settle a decision, they can see the part of its downside that reflow2 can compute from the design: how much built work (capabilities realized, files registered) and checked work (passing verifications) lies downstream of what the decision governs, and how many recorded decisions it rests on. That is what a reversal would have to unwind.

reflow2 shows only what it can count. How likely the decision is to be wrong, and how much it gains if right, stay the person's judgement, and reflow2 never turns them into a score.

Where the decision-to-decision chain is mostly unrecorded, the reply says so rather than reporting a soft design. Measured 2026-09-06 on reflow2's own design: 157 of 193 accepted decisions rested on no recorded decision, so a layer count alone would read "easy to undo" for nearly everything.

Via negativa (rule:before-a-structural-addition-ask-what-could-be-taken-away): no new tool and no schema change. The downstream walk is the one propagate_from already makes, and the count of what hangs off a decision is what what_next's shaping band already computes. This requirement puts them in front of the person at the moment of deciding.
